To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

diaminopurinyl-PNA oligomers form more stable and selective duplexes with complementary DNA, and that a diaminopuranine-PNA oligomer forms a strand-displacement complex with a double-stranded DNA target.
the substitution of adenine by the isomeric diaminopurin in PNA oligomer increases the Tm of duplexes formed by complementary DNA, RNA and PNA by 3-6 degrees C per diamino-purine.
the substitution of diaminopurin in PNA oligonucleotides results in increased T m of DNA and RNA duplexes and improved sequence discrimination against mismatches in the DNA and RNA strand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of PNA oligomer analogues that have improved hybridizing properties.
the development of a PNA monomer containing 2, 6-diaminourine and the synthesis of PNA oligomeres containing diaminourine.
the development of PNA analogs that bind DNA more strongly and discriminate more effectively against mismatches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diaminopuranine is a very good replacement for the adenine residue in PNA, and that this modification is of great interest for the development of new applications for PNA.

the incorporation of diaminopurinyl nucleobases into PNA oligomeric sequences increases the thermal stability of the duplexes formed with the complementary nucleic acid sequences and also increases the specificity of binding.
the introduction of diaminopurinyl nucleobases into PNA oligonucleotides results in an improved binding affinity for complementary DNA or RNA.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PNA oligomers incorporating 2,6-DAP can form more stable duplexes with complementary DNA, as well as discriminate against mismatches, and can form stable complexes with target sequences.
the diaminopurnine modification of PNA can be incorporated into oligomers and that this modification increases the Tm of duplexes formed by PNA and DNA, RNA, or other PNA.
the incorporation of diaminopurinyl nucleosides into PNA increases the T m of PNA-DNA and PNA-RNA hybrid formation and improves sequence discrimination.
